newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour warns water firms "enough is enough".
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour warns water firms "enough is enough".

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party on Monday stepped up its attacks on the privatised water industry, accusing it of amassing "floods of cash" and giving consumers nothing but "floods of excuses".

Publishing its 1996 annual report on the industry, the party said that water privatisation in 1989 had short-changed both consumers and the environment, forcing up prices while allowing the firms to accumulate 11.1 billion stg of profits.
A Labour Government would levy a windfall tax on the companies' bumper earnings and ensure that they operate to the benefit of customers and the environment, it said.

Frank Dobson, Labour's environment spokesman, said water leakage had risen, there were three prosecutions per month of water companies on pollution charges and investment had fallen by 361 million pounds.
"But water privatisation had been good for profits...and dividends, which have totalled 3.5 billion stg," Dobson said.
"Water privatisation has been better still for water company bosses, who have voted themselves over 20 million stg in pay and perks. Enough is enough."

Dobson said water prices had risen by 40 percent since privatisation, while the number of interruptions of supply had risen -- with those lasting more than 12 hours doubling to over 130,000 last year alone.
Unlike electricity prices, water charges have risen since privatisation, partly because of new, more stringent European Union directives on the quality of drinking and swimming water.
